note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Look for a tall perennial tuft and a broadly branched 15–40 cm panicle, often reddish-purple while flowering and tan after maturity. Panels 0–1 show different color phases. Do not identify purpletop by color, sticky branch feel or bare lower panicle branches alone: Texas tridens can share those cues. Archived Bob Harms panel 9 additionally shows attached flowering branchlets; do not infer individual lemma anatomy from it.
tiles.short: Large open, often drooping flowering panicle
tiles.status: VISIBLE HEAD SHAPE; CONNECTED ROOTED PLANT GAP

tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK THE FLATTENED BASAL SHEATHS
tiles.details: Purpletop often has compressed, keeled and overlapping lower sheaths, producing a two-sided base; Texas A&M and Flora of North Central Texas describe this conspicuous vegetative cue. Culms commonly 60–180 cm and the crown can have short rhizomes. Photograph the intact attached lower sheaths from front and side with centimeter scale; do not infer the shape from distant flowering-head images or dig just to prove rhizomes. Confirm with the open panicle and ripe spikelets because base shape alone is not species-diagnostic.
tiles.short: Look for overlapping, laterally flattened/keeled lower sheaths on the perennial crown
tiles.status: PUBLISHED BASAL SHEATH CUE — NO ATTACHED BASE PHOTO YET

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE INNER COLLAR
tiles.details: Expose the actual inner blade/sheath junction at 10–20×. Go Botany describes a hair-type ligule up to 0.5 mm; a conspicuous fringe of longer white hairs can occur on the collar itself. Do not label longer collar hairs as the ligule or imply that the current gallery has a measured collar macro. Archived Bob Harms panel 7 now supplies a genuine source-labelled collar/ligule-region photograph, but does not independently resolve or measure the tiny free ligule margin.
tiles.status: REAL COLLAR PHOTO; CALIBRATED LIGULE STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · COUNT THE FLORETS
tiles.details: The archived Matt Lavin panel 2 shows a real intact purpletop spikelet with overlapping florets, but not a verified millimeter scale or individual dissected glume/lemma identity. Botanical treatments report spikelets about 5–10 mm with commonly 4–8 florets; count the florets inside ONE ripe spikelet. Bob Harms panel 8 also photographs detached reproductive parts beside a metric reference; organ-by-organ glume/lemma assignments and measurements have not been independently verified.
tiles.status: TWO REAL REPRODUCTIVE PHOTOS; INDIVIDUAL PART VALIDATION PENDING

tiles.heading: 05 · TWO GLUMES AND A HAIRY LEMMA
tiles.details: Published purpletop anatomy: lower 1-veined glume approximately 2.5–3 mm, upper 1-veined glume about 3.5–4 mm. Fertile lemma approximately 3–5 mm, three-veined with hairs along lower portions of veins and a two-toothed apex; the central nerve may project as a minute mucro to ~0.5 mm, NOT a long awn. These values are not measurements from panel 2; separate the organs before arrowing. The archived Bob Harms panel 8 is a real detached-parts photograph with metric reference, not proof that the glume vein counts, lemma hairs, paired teeth or mucro can be resolved. No fine arrows should be added without pixel verification.
tiles.status: REAL DETACHED-PARTS PHOTO; VEINS/HAIRS/MUCRO NOT CERTIFIED

tiles.heading: 06 · COMPARE TEXAS AND WHITE TRIDENS
tiles.details: Panels 3–4 show white tridens (T. albescens) with contracted crowded heads; panels 5–6 show Texas tridens (T. texanus) with a generally shorter flexuous panicle. Both purpletop and Texas tridens can have exposed proximal branch sections and rosy spikelets. Compare mature glume/lemma lengths and hairy lemma nerves when gross architecture overlaps. Check purpletop's flattened keeled overlapping basal sheaths on the same attached plant as an additional field cue; do not assume this trait alone excludes Texas tridens. When the flowering head is old/tan, verify actual multi-flowered spikelets rather than relying on purple color or sticky branches.
tiles.status: FIELD LOOK-ALIKE CUE; MATCHED MACROS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: PURPLETOP: first find a tall perennial with a broad open, often drooping panicle (purple in bloom or tan later). THEN inspect the LOWER SHEATHS: the flattened, overlapping, keeled bases often give the crown a two-sided, compressed appearance (Texas A&M; Flora of North Central Texas). This is a supporting field character, not species-proof. Bare lower panicle branches and pink spikelets also occur in Texas tridens; confirm the true very short hair-fringe ligule and measured glumes/lemma before a final ID.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: See the first SOURCE-LABELLED PHOTO: use gross branches and spikelets as starting clues, not independent expert taxon confirmation.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Purpletop often has compressed, keeled and overlapping lower sheaths, producing a two-sided base; Texas A&M and Flora of North Central Texas describe this conspicuous vegetative cue. Culms commonly 60–180 cm and the crown can have short rhizomes. Photograph the intact attached lower sheaths from front and side with centimeter scale; do not infer the shape from distant flowering-head images or dig just to prove rhizomes. Confirm with the open panicle and ripe spikelets because base shape alone is not species-diagnostic.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Published purpletop anatomy: lower 1-veined glume approximately 2.5–3 mm, upper 1-veined glume about 3.5–4 mm. Fertile lemma approximately 3–5 mm, three-veined with hairs along lower portions of veins and a two-toothed apex; the central nerve may project as a minute mucro to ~0.5 mm, NOT a long awn. These values are not measurements from panel 2; separate the organs before arrowing. The archived Bob Harms panel 8 is a real detached-parts photograph with metric reference, not proof that the glume vein counts, lemma hairs, paired teeth or mucro can be resolved. No fine arrows should be added without pixel verification.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Against T. texanus, don't use bare lower panicle branches as unique: both species have them; compare total spread, culm size and measured glumes/lemma. Against T. albescens, widely open flower-bearing branches versus tightly appressed contracted branches are strong first clues. Purple is not required: this second source photo is straw-colored.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: 3 · SPIKELET MICRO — actual multi-flowered purpletop head and separated parts · PROVISIONAL REVIEW
panels.caption: Matt Lavin's 668×704 close-up has the entire purpletop spikelet with several nested florets on the RIGHT; LEFT and CENTER are detached parts. Source was labelled Tridens flavus. Without a measurement or attached pre-dissection sequence we cannot say which tiny individual part is the upper glume, lemma, or palea.
panels.creator: Matt Lavin
panels.modifications: Original CC BY-SA 2.0 source resized zero pixels (668x704); clean RGB JPEG metadata/GPS removed, no crop. Arrows are browser overlays, original attribution preserved.
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: White tridens — green contracted spike
panels.caption: Original source-labelled flowering head shows an extremely narrow, dense, upright panicle with overlapping pale-green spikelets; this view cannot resolve lemma nerve hairs, basal ligule or exact measurements.
panels.creator: Sam Kieschnick
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: Texas tridens — arching mature seedhead
panels.caption: Existing public-domain specimen image shows an arched central panicle axis, flexuous slender lateral branches, spikelet-free proximal branch sections, and terminal hanging spikelet groups. Neither a compact spike nor lemma hair detail is visible.
panels.creator: Gaiacoyote

memory_rule: ALBESCENS narrow packed; FLAVUS wide drooping; TEXANUS flexuous separated. Confirm at mature GLUMES and 3-NERVED LEMMA.
safety_note: Bare panicle branch bases are not unique to Texas tridens. Source-labelled photos do not establish unreviewed county nativity.
field_rule: Species-level Tridens confidence requires panicle architecture PLUS mature spikelet/glume/lemma anatomy; do not identify from pigmentation alone.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
